en: Sura 68: Al-Qalam

p.src: 68:1  Nūn[1]. By the pen and what they [i.e., the angels] write [in the Records of deeds],

ar: بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ نٓ ۚ وَٱلْقَلَمِ وَمَا يَسْطُرُونَ
en: Nūn[1]. By the pen and what they [i.e., the angels] write [in the Records of deeds],
u.src: 68:1  Nūn[1]. By the pen and what they [i.e., the angels] write [in the Records of deeds],

en: [1] See footnote 2:1.

p.src: 68:2  By the grace of your Lord [O Prophet], you are not a madman.

en: By the grace of your Lord [O Prophet], you are not a madman.
u.src: 68:2  By the grace of your Lord [O Prophet], you are not a madman.

p.src: 68:3  You will surely have a never-ending reward.

en: You will surely have a never-ending reward.
u.src: 68:3  You will surely have a never-ending reward.

p.src: 68:4  Indeed, you are of a great moral character.

en: Indeed, you are of a great moral character.
u.src: 68:4  Indeed, you are of a great moral character.

p.src: 68:5  Soon you will see and they will see,

en: Soon you will see and they will see,
u.src: 68:5  Soon you will see and they will see,

p.src: 68:6  which of you is afflicted with madness.

en: which of you is afflicted with madness.
u.src: 68:6  which of you is afflicted with madness.

p.src: 68:7  Indeed, your Lord alone knows best who has strayed from His way and those who are rightly guided.

ar: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَن ضَلَّ عَن سَبِيلِهِۦ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِٱلْمُهْتَدِينَ
en: Indeed, your Lord alone knows best who has strayed from His way and those who are rightly guided.
u.src: 68:7  Indeed, your Lord alone knows best who has strayed from His way and those who are rightly guided.

p.src: 68:8  So do not obey the deniers.

en: So do not obey the deniers.
u.src: 68:8  So do not obey the deniers.

p.src: 68:9  They wish that you would compromise so they would too compromise.

en: They wish that you would compromise so they would too compromise.
u.src: 68:9  They wish that you would compromise so they would too compromise.

p.src: 68:10  And do not obey every disgraceful swearer,

en: And do not obey every disgraceful swearer,
u.src: 68:10  And do not obey every disgraceful swearer,

p.src: 68:11  backbiter, gossip-monger,

en: backbiter, gossip-monger,
u.src: 68:11  backbiter, gossip-monger,

p.src: 68:12  withholder of good, transgressor, sinful,

en: withholder of good, transgressor, sinful,
u.src: 68:12  withholder of good, transgressor, sinful,

p.src: 68:13  coarse, and furthermore, an illegitimate child[2].

en: coarse, and furthermore, an illegitimate child[2].
u.src: 68:13  coarse, and furthermore, an illegitimate child[2].

en: [2] i.e., falsely claiming a particular lineage. It refers to Al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah (See also 74:11-25) or possibly Al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq.

p.src: 68:14  Simply because he has wealth and children,

en: Simply because he has wealth and children,
u.src: 68:14  Simply because he has wealth and children,

p.src: 68:15  When Our verses are recited to him, he says, “Ancient fables!”

ar: إِذَا تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِ ءَايَـٰتُنَا قَالَ أَسَـٰطِيرُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
en: When Our verses are recited to him, he says, “Ancient fables!”
u.src: 68:15  When Our verses are recited to him, he says, “Ancient fables!”

p.src: 68:16  We will soon brand him on the snout[3].

en: We will soon brand him on the snout[3].
u.src: 68:16  We will soon brand him on the snout[3].

en: [3] Lit., "trunk," meaning the nose of an elephant or pig. These verses refer to Al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah, a leader of the pagans of Makkah and a staunch enemy of Islam. He called the Prophet (ﷺ) a madman, so the Qur’an responded by mentioning ten of Al-Walīd’s qualities. (See 53:33-35 and 74:11-26). Two of those qualities were not known to him: the fact that he was an illegitimate child and that his nose would be chopped off years later at the Battle of Badr. Khālid ibn al-Walīd and two of his brothers embraced Islam.

p.src: 68:17  Indeed, We have tested them [i.e., the Makkans] as We tested the people of the garden when they swore to harvest its fruits in the early morning,

ar: إِنَّا بَلَوْنَـٰهُمْ كَمَا بَلَوْنَآ أَصْحَـٰبَ ٱلْجَنَّةِ إِذْ أَقْسَمُوا۟ لَيَصْرِمُنَّهَا مُصْبِحِينَ
en: Indeed, We have tested them [i.e., the Makkans] as We tested the people of the garden when they swore to harvest its fruits in the early morning,
u.src: 68:17  Indeed, We have tested them [i.e., the Makkans] as We tested the people of the garden when they swore to harvest its fruits in the early morning,

p.src: 68:18  and made no exception [by saying: if Allah wills][4].

en: and made no exception [by saying: if Allah wills][4].
u.src: 68:18  and made no exception [by saying: if Allah wills][4].

en: [4] Or without leaving some for the poor.

p.src: 68:19  Then it was struck by an affliction from your Lord while they were asleep,

ar: فَطَافَ عَلَيْهَا طَآئِفٌ مِّن رَّبِّكَ وَهُمْ نَآئِمُونَ
en: Then it was struck by an affliction from your Lord while they were asleep,
u.src: 68:19  Then it was struck by an affliction from your Lord while they were asleep,

p.src: 68:20  and it turned to ashes [as black as night].

en: and it turned to ashes [as black as night].
u.src: 68:20  and it turned to ashes [as black as night].

p.src: 68:21  Then in the early morning they called out to one another:

en: Then in the early morning they called out to one another:
u.src: 68:21  Then in the early morning they called out to one another:

p.src: 68:22  “Go early to your garden if you really wish to harvest.”

ar: أَنِ ٱغْدُوا۟ عَلَىٰ حَرْثِكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ صَـٰرِمِينَ
en: “Go early to your garden if you really wish to harvest.”
u.src: 68:22  “Go early to your garden if you really wish to harvest.”

p.src: 68:23  So they set out, whispering to one another,

en: So they set out, whispering to one another,
u.src: 68:23  So they set out, whispering to one another,

p.src: 68:24  “Not a single poor person should enter your garden today.”

ar: أَن لَّا يَدْخُلَنَّهَا ٱلْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكُم مِّسْكِينٌ
en: “Not a single poor person should enter your garden today.”
u.src: 68:24  “Not a single poor person should enter your garden today.”

p.src: 68:25  And they left early, fully determined to stick to their plan[5].

en: And they left early, fully determined to stick to their plan[5].
u.src: 68:25  And they left early, fully determined to stick to their plan[5].

en: [5] To implement their plan, fully confident of their ability.

p.src: 68:26  But when they saw the garden, they said, “We must have lost our way!

en: But when they saw the garden, they said, “We must have lost our way!
u.src: 68:26  But when they saw the garden, they said, “We must have lost our way!

p.src: 68:27  Rather, we have been deprived.”

en: Rather, we have been deprived.”
u.src: 68:27  Rather, we have been deprived.”

p.src: 68:28  The best among them said, “Did I not say to you to glorify Allah[6]?”

ar: قَالَ أَوْسَطُهُمْ أَلَمْ أَقُل لَّكُمْ لَوْلَا تُسَبِّحُونَ
en: The best among them said, “Did I not say to you to glorify Allah[6]?”
u.src: 68:28  The best among them said, “Did I not say to you to glorify Allah[6]?”

en: [6] i.e., remember Him by saying, "...if Allah wills." Or "praise" and "thank" Allah for His bounty.

p.src: 68:29  They said, “Glory be to our Lord! We were truly wrongdoers.”

ar: قَالُوا۟ سُبْحَـٰنَ رَبِّنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَـٰلِمِينَ
en: They said, “Glory be to our Lord! We were truly wrongdoers.”
u.src: 68:29  They said, “Glory be to our Lord! We were truly wrongdoers.”

p.src: 68:30  Then they turned to one another, throwing blame.

en: Then they turned to one another, throwing blame.
u.src: 68:30  Then they turned to one another, throwing blame.

p.src: 68:31  They said, “Woe to us! We were surely transgressors.

en: They said, “Woe to us! We were surely transgressors.
u.src: 68:31  They said, “Woe to us! We were surely transgressors.

p.src: 68:32  Our Lord may give us something better than this. We certainly turn to our Lord in hope[7].”

ar: عَسَىٰ رَبُّنَآ أَن يُبْدِلَنَا خَيْرًا مِّنْهَآ إِنَّآ إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا رَٰغِبُونَ
en: Our Lord may give us something better than this. We certainly turn to our Lord in hope[7].”
u.src: 68:32  Our Lord may give us something better than this. We certainly turn to our Lord in hope[7].”

en: [7] Of His forgiveness and bounty.

p.src: 68:33  Such is the punishment [in this world]; but the punishment of the Hereafter is far worse, if only they knew.

ar: كَذَٰلِكَ ٱلْعَذَابُ ۖ وَلَعَذَابُ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ أَكْبَرُ ۚ لَوْ كَانُوا۟ يَعْلَمُونَ
en: Such is the punishment [in this world]; but the punishment of the Hereafter is far worse, if only they knew.
u.src: 68:33  Such is the punishment [in this world]; but the punishment of the Hereafter is far worse, if only they knew.

p.src: 68:34  Indeed, the righteous will have gardens of bliss with their Lord.

ar: إِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنَّـٰتِ ٱلنَّعِيمِ
en: Indeed, the righteous will have gardens of bliss with their Lord.
u.src: 68:34  Indeed, the righteous will have gardens of bliss with their Lord.

p.src: 68:35  Should We then treat Muslims like the wicked?

en: Should We then treat Muslims like the wicked?
u.src: 68:35  Should We then treat Muslims like the wicked?

p.src: 68:36  What is the matter with you that you make such a judgment?

en: What is the matter with you that you make such a judgment?
u.src: 68:36  What is the matter with you that you make such a judgment?

p.src: 68:37  Or do you have a scripture in which you read

en: Or do you have a scripture in which you read
u.src: 68:37  Or do you have a scripture in which you read

p.src: 68:38  that you will be given whatever you choose?

en: that you will be given whatever you choose?
u.src: 68:38  that you will be given whatever you choose?

p.src: 68:39  Or do you have a solemn promise binding upon Us until the Day of Resurrection, that you will have whatever you decide for yourselves?

ar: أَمْ لَكُمْ أَيْمَـٰنٌ عَلَيْنَا بَـٰلِغَةٌ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَـٰمَةِ ۙ إِنَّ لَكُمْ لَمَا تَحْكُمُونَ
en: Or do you have a solemn promise binding upon Us until the Day of Resurrection, that you will have whatever you decide for yourselves?
u.src: 68:39  Or do you have a solemn promise binding upon Us until the Day of Resurrection, that you will have whatever you decide for yourselves?

p.src: 68:40  Ask them which of them can guarantee that.

en: Ask them which of them can guarantee that.
u.src: 68:40  Ask them which of them can guarantee that.

p.src: 68:41  Or do they have associate-gods? Then let them bring forth their associate-gods[8], if they are truthful.

ar: أَمْ لَهُمْ شُرَكَآءُ فَلْيَأْتُوا۟ بِشُرَكَآئِهِمْ إِن كَانُوا۟ صَـٰدِقِينَ
en: Or do they have associate-gods? Then let them bring forth their associate-gods[8], if they are truthful.
u.src: 68:41  Or do they have associate-gods? Then let them bring forth their associate-gods[8], if they are truthful.

en: [8] whom they took as partners with Allah.

p.src: 68:42  On the Day when the Shin [of Allah] will be uncovered[9], and they are invited to prostrate, but they will not be able to do so.

ar: يَوْمَ يُكْشَفُ عَن سَاقٍ وَيُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى ٱلسُّجُودِ فَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ
en: On the Day when the Shin [of Allah] will be uncovered[9], and they are invited to prostrate, but they will not be able to do so.
u.src: 68:42  On the Day when the Shin [of Allah] will be uncovered[9], and they are invited to prostrate, but they will not be able to do so.

en: [9] i.e., It is a Day that everyone will find before him great difficulty. According to a long and authentic Hadīth of Abu Sa‘īd al-Khudrī, "the Shin" refers to that of Allah Almighty, before which every believer will prostrate on the Day of Judgment when the disbelievers and hypocrites will not be able to prostrate. The text of the Hadith is as follows: "... Then the Lord will uncover His Shank, so they will prostrate to Him...".

p.src: 68:43  Their eyes will be downcast, overwhelmed with humiliation, for they were invited to prostrate when they were capable[10] [but they refused].

ar: خَـٰشِعَةً أَبْصَـٰرُهُمْ تَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌ ۖ وَقَدْ كَانُوا۟ يُدْعَوْنَ إِلَى ٱلسُّجُودِ وَهُمْ سَـٰلِمُونَ
en: Their eyes will be downcast, overwhelmed with humiliation, for they were invited to prostrate when they were capable[10] [but they refused].
u.src: 68:43  Their eyes will be downcast, overwhelmed with humiliation, for they were invited to prostrate when they were capable[10] [but they refused].

en: [10] During the life of this world.

p.src: 68:44  So leave to Me those who reject this message [O Prophet]. We will gradually lead them to their ruin in ways that they do not perceive[11].

ar: فَذَرْنِى وَمَن يُكَذِّبُ بِهَـٰذَا ٱلْحَدِيثِ ۖ سَنَسْتَدْرِجُهُم مِّنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
en: So leave to Me those who reject this message [O Prophet]. We will gradually lead them to their ruin in ways that they do not perceive[11].
u.src: 68:44  So leave to Me those who reject this message [O Prophet]. We will gradually lead them to their ruin in ways that they do not perceive[11].

en: [11] Allah will increase favors upon them in this life as a trial, so they will increase sin, which will lead to their destruction.

p.src: 68:45  I will give them respite, but My plan is firm.

en: I will give them respite, but My plan is firm.
u.src: 68:45  I will give them respite, but My plan is firm.

p.src: 68:46  Or are you asking them for a reward, so they find it too burdensome?

ar: أَمْ تَسْـَٔلُهُمْ أَجْرًا فَهُم مِّن مَّغْرَمٍ مُّثْقَلُونَ
en: Or are you asking them for a reward, so they find it too burdensome?
u.src: 68:46  Or are you asking them for a reward, so they find it too burdensome?

p.src: 68:47  Or do they have knowledge of the unseen, so they write it down?

en: Or do they have knowledge of the unseen, so they write it down?
u.src: 68:47  Or do they have knowledge of the unseen, so they write it down?

p.src: 68:48  So be patient with the decree of your Lord, and do not be like the man of the Whale [i.e., Jonah], when he cried out in anguish[12].

ar: فَٱصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ وَلَا تَكُن كَصَاحِبِ ٱلْحُوتِ إِذْ نَادَىٰ وَهُوَ مَكْظُومٌ
en: So be patient with the decree of your Lord, and do not be like the man of the Whale [i.e., Jonah], when he cried out in anguish[12].
u.src: 68:48  So be patient with the decree of your Lord, and do not be like the man of the Whale [i.e., Jonah], when he cried out in anguish[12].

en: [12] While inside the belly of the whale. See 21:87 and 37:139-148.

p.src: 68:49  Had it not been for the grace that he received from his Lord, he would have surely been thrown onto the barren shore, blameworthy[13].

ar: لَّوْلَآ أَن تَدَٰرَكَهُۥ نِعْمَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِۦ لَنُبِذَ بِٱلْعَرَآءِ وَهُوَ مَذْمُومٌ
en: Had it not been for the grace that he received from his Lord, he would have surely been thrown onto the barren shore, blameworthy[13].
u.src: 68:49  Had it not been for the grace that he received from his Lord, he would have surely been thrown onto the barren shore, blameworthy[13].

en: [13] Instead, Allah accepted his repentance and provided for him means of recovery. See 37:139-148.

p.src: 68:50  But his Lord chose him and made him one of the righteous.

en: But his Lord chose him and made him one of the righteous.
u.src: 68:50  But his Lord chose him and made him one of the righteous.

p.src: 68:51  The disbelievers would almost strike you down with their malicious gazes when they hear the Reminder, and they say, “He is certainly mad.”

ar: وَإِن يَكَادُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ لَيُزْلِقُونَكَ بِأَبْصَـٰرِهِمْ لَمَّا سَمِعُوا۟ ٱلذِّكْرَ وَيَقُولُونَ إِنَّهُۥ لَمَجْنُونٌ
en: The disbelievers would almost strike you down with their malicious gazes when they hear the Reminder, and they say, “He is certainly mad.”
u.src: 68:51  The disbelievers would almost strike you down with their malicious gazes when they hear the Reminder, and they say, “He is certainly mad.”

p.src: 68:52  But it is nothing other than a reminder to the whole world.

en: But it is nothing other than a reminder to the whole world.
u.src: 68:52  But it is nothing other than a reminder to the whole world.
